x: The policy document (and AddPermission/RemovePermission statements) is stored and returned exactly as written, but Vyomi never evaluates it — it is never consulted to allow or deny a Publish, Subscribe, or management call.

Publish bodies are scanned against the policy's Inbound statements for a representative, regex-based subset of data identifiers (email addresses, credit card numbers, US Social Security numbers, IP addresses) and Deny/Deidentify/Audit are really enforced (Deny blocks the Publish, Deidentify masks the match before fan-out, Audit is recorded in the delivery log) — but Vyomi doesn't implement AWS's full ML-backed managed data-identifier catalog, and Outbound (post-delivery) statements are never evaluated.

The per-topic/per-subscription HTTP/S retry policy (healthyRetryPolicy — numRetries, min/maxDelayTarget, backoffFunction, numNoDelayRetries/numMinDelayRetries/numMaxDelayRetries, disableSubscriptionOverrides) is really enforced: the offline appliance's delivery worker retries a failing HTTP/S endpoint over the real network exactly that many times on that backoff curve before redriving the message to the subscription's RedrivePolicy dead-letter queue. On Nano/dev_server there is no durable delivery worker, so an HTTP/S push is never actually sent (see sns.publish.other-protocols) — but the same policy still drives how many DeliveryFailure attempts are recorded and whether the exhausted message lands in the dead-letter queue, computed synchronously instead of over real elapsed time.

features.t: Delivery status logging (CloudWatch Logs feedback for successful/failed deliveries)
x: Setting {Protocol}SuccessFeedbackRoleArn / SuccessFeedbackSampleRate / FailureFeedbackRoleArn is real, and Vyomi really writes a CloudWatch Logs delivery-status record (notification/delivery/status, sample-rated) to a sns/<region>/<account-id>/<topic-name>/Success|Failure log group it creates — but only for Amazon SQS subscriptions, since Nano has no durable delivery worker to know the HTTP/Lambda/Firehose/platform-endpoint outcome synchronously; Vyomi never creates or checks the IAM role named in the role ARN.

The KmsMasterKeyId attribute round-trips through SetTopicAttributes/GetTopicAttributes, but Vyomi does not actually encrypt stored message bodies with it, and the console only offers the default AWS managed key — there is no customer-key picker.

features.t: Subscription filter policies (message attributes and message body scope)

x: The RedrivePolicy attribute round-trips and is honoured for SQS/HTTP/Lambda/email push failures, but on Nano (no durable delivery workers) only SQS and HTTP/S subscriptions can actually exhaust retries and land in the dead-letter queue within a single session (HTTP/S synchronously, running the subscription's own healthyRetryPolicy schedule to completion — see sns.topic.delivery-policy); Lambda/email redrive still requires the offline appliance's delivery workers.

features.t: Publish fan-out to subscribed Amazon SQS queues (filter policies, raw delivery, FIFO)
Publish fan-out to HTTP/S, AWS Lambda, and email subscriptions
x: On Nano (and the dev server) there is no durable delivery worker, so deliveries to HTTP/S, Lambda, and email endpoints are recorded in the subscription's retry-policy accounting but never actually sent — only the native SubscriptionConfirmation/Notification shape is proven. The offline appliance really performs the HTTP POST (with the SNS signature and SubscribeURL handshake), invokes the Lambda function, and sends the email through its local SMTP relay.

Vyomi has no real carrier/SMPP gateway, so SMS is never actually delivered — Publish only succeeds against a phone number that has gone through the sandbox verification flow, and the send is recorded, not transmitted.

features.t: Mobile push platform applications and endpoints
x: Creating, listing, updating and deleting platform applications and endpoints is real and stateful (tokens, attributes, enablement), but Vyomi has no real APNS/FCM/ADM gateway to reach, so no push notification is ever actually delivered to a device.

features.t: Mobile push delivery (push gateway stub: inbox + webhook)
x: Real: Publish to a platform endpoint builds the platform-native payload (APNS aps.alert, GCM/FCM/ADM data, or your own per-platform JSON with MessageStructure=json) and the push gateway stub delivers it to the endpoint's device inbox (VyomiListPushInbox, shown on the Push notifications page); on the offline appliance it also POSTs it to the endpoint's VyomiPushWebhook attribute, and a 404/410 answer disables the endpoint like APNS/FCM rejecting a token. It is never sent to real APNS, FCM or ADM (no Apple/Google credentials); Nano has no sockets, so it delivers to the inbox only.

features.t: SMS account attributes (default type, spend limit, sample rate, logging role, usage report bucket, sender ID)
x: SetSMSAttributes/GetSMSAttributes round-trip exactly as set, and MonthlySpendLimit is really enforced — Publish to a phone number is denied once accumulated spend reaches the configured limit — but the per-message cost is a flat estimate, not real carrier billing rates, and Vyomi never writes delivery-status logs or S3 usage reports.

Adding, listing, and deleting sandbox numbers is real and stateful, and a number must be verified before Publish will send to it — but Vyomi can't deliver the real verification SMS, so the one-time code has to be read from the backend state rather than a text message.

Statistics are the real AWS/SNS CloudWatch metrics (NumberOfNotificationsDelivered, SMSSuccessRate, SMSMonthToDateSpentUSD; aggregate and per Country derived from the E.164 calling code) of every SMS this environment accepted. Vyomi has no carrier, so each accepted message counts as delivered into its own delivery log and the success rate is always 100%.

features.t: SMS verification code delivery (simulated handset inbox)
x: Vyomi has no carrier or handset, so no text reaches a real phone. Every SMS the simulator sends (sandbox verification codes, Publish to a verified phone, SMS topic subscriptions) is delivered to a simulated handset inbox instead, readable through the Vyomi-only VyomiListSimulatedSMS action and shown in the console's Verify phone number dialog. Real AWS has no API to read the code back.

Real Amazon SNS has no per-topic size setting - its payload limit is fixed (256 KiB here). Vyomi adds the topic attribute VyomiMaximumMessageSize (1-262144 bytes, SetTopicAttributes / the console field) as an extension: Publish and PublishBatch of a larger message (body + attribute names/types/values) fail with InvalidParameter 'Message too long'. SQS subscriptions additionally honour the destination queue's own MaximumMessageSize. Real SDKs/CLIs that never set the extension are unaffected.

The real TTL is the push message attribute AWS.SNS.MOBILE.<PLATFORM>.TTL (0-2419200 seconds, validated on Publish exactly so). Vyomi has no mobile push service, so the TTL is applied to the deliveries it does retry (HTTP/S, Lambda, email workers on the offline appliance; the synchronous healthyRetryPolicy simulation on Nano): once the TTL elapses no further retry is made and the message is dropped to the subscription's dead-letter queue. SQS deliveries are immediate, so TTL has no effect on them.

features.t: Topic Integrations tab (EventBridge rules, CloudWatch alarms and Lambda/SQS/Firehose subscriptions wired to the topic)
x: A live read-only view assembled from real data: EventBridge rules whose target is the topic (ListRuleNamesByTarget across buses), CloudWatch alarms with the topic as an alarm action, and the topic's subscriptions grouped by protocol. SNS itself has no 'integrations' API, so nothing is stored — links open the real EventBridge/CloudWatch wizards. EventBridge Pipes sources and Firehose delivery-stream creation from this tab are not modeled.
